strategy_title: Increasing XBLOCK via Autotune Causes 4x Instruction Blowup
strategy_description: Increasing the tile size (XBLOCK) from 128 to 512 via autotune improved scheduler eligibility (No Eligible dropped from 40.5% to 16.6%) and achieved occupancy (55.7% → 78.5%), but caused a 4x increase in total executed instructions (4.6M → 18.4M) and 2.4x longer kernel duration (12.3 µs → 30.1 µs). The regression was caused by a critical implementation flaw: the grid was not updated to use `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)` — it remained hardcoded at `triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128)`, so with XBLOCK=512 the grid launched 4x too many CTAs, each processing the same data redundantly. When adding autotune to change XBLOCK, the launch grid MUST be a dynamic lambda that reads `meta['XBLOCK']`, not a static expression computed with the old tile size.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=128, grid hardcoded
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # 15680 blocks
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=512, but grid still hardcoded to old value — BUG
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # still 15680 blocks — should be 3920!
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=512)  # each element processed 4x
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern (static grid + autotune XBLOCK). Always pair autotune XBLOCK changes with a dynamic grid lambda.
do_not_apply_when: Any time the launch grid is computed statically using the old XBLOCK value — this will cause redundant work proportional to the tile size ratio and always regress performance.
framework_notes: In Triton, when using @triton.autotune to vary XBLOCK, the grid must be `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)`. A static grid expression like `(triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)` does NOT update when autotune selects a different XBLOCK, causing over-launch and 4x+ instruction blowup.
